your_book:
Jaleel's book had a mixed Tuesday, with the headline number — a 6.2% overall unrealized gain — holding steady beneath a split tape. Abbott (ABT, 10.7% weight) was the standout mover, up 2.09% on the session and sitting on a 30.3% gain; it remains the largest position and continues to earn its keep despite the mild EPS-guide trim flagged earlier this summer. Adobe (ADBE, 5.2%) surged 3.58% — the best day-move in the book — likely carried by broader software sentiment and M&A chatter around peers like Workday. Gilead (GILD) added 3.25% and Equifax (EFX) 2.85%, though both are small weights so their contribution is limited. On the other side, Rocket Lab (RKLB, 7.8%) fell 3.56% and NVIDIA (NVDA, 5.7%) dropped 2.34%, with AVGO off 3.17% — the semiconductor complex taking heat from rising yields and inflation jitters. Boston Scientific (BSX, 9.5%) slid 1.87%, a name already carrying an elevated risk flag after its FY26 growth guide was slashed to 7–8.5%.

The drift story worth watching: BSX is rated STRONG BUY with a QARP of 73, yet the thesis — durable med-device comps — is being actively undermined by management's own flat-through-Q3 guidance. Price and thesis are pulling in opposite directions, and Tuesday's decline adds to a gain of only 3.0% from cost. Similarly, LULU bounced 2.83% today but is still underwater at –6.9% and carries a guidance-cut flag with Americas comps down five straight quarters. A single green session doesn't repair that thesis. RKLB remains the most glaring structural mismatch: an AVOID verdict and a QARP of 36.7 at 7.8% of the book — the second-largest weight in a capital-preservation mandate — with another –3.56% session to show for it.

Looking ahead, NVDA's next catalyst is August 26 — less than two weeks out — and the stock is already rattled by export-control headlines and an opinion piece openly questioning AI-capex sustainability. The ServiceNow (NOW) headline flagging business-model risk is noise until proven otherwise, but at 6.1% weight and a high multiple, it warrants monitoring ahead of its October 27 print. ADBE's next report is September 10; the narrative risk (AI disruption, CFO exit) hasn't gone away even after today's pop.

attention.headline: AVOID-rated name at near-top weight, down again today
attention.note: RKLB carries the book's lowest QARP (36.7), an explicit AVOID verdict, and shed another 3.56% Tuesday — yet at 7.8% it is the second-largest single position in a capital-preservation book, a direct contradiction that demands resolution.

attention.headline: Guidance slashed; price and thesis diverging
attention.note: Management guided flat through Q3 after cutting FY26 growth to 7–8.5%, yet the STRONG BUY verdict and 9.5% weight assume a durable growth story — Tuesday's –1.87% move and a cumulative gain of only 3.0% suggest the market is not buying that story.

attention.headline: Earnings eight days out; export-control and AI-capex narrative heating up
attention.note: NVDA fell 2.34% Tuesday against a backdrop of tightening China export licenses and a prominent 'AI bubble' headline — with the August 26 print imminent, the risk flag could crystallize quickly.

attention.headline: Big pop today, but AI-disruption narrative unresolved ahead of Sep 10 report
attention.note: Today's 3.58% gain looks like sentiment relief rather than a fundamental reset — the CFO exit, AI-moat concerns, and ARR de-emphasis haven't been answered, and September 10 will force the issue.
